STEVEN H. WHITE

I write from lived experience—and for the people who live beside addiction.

After nearly twenty years of drinking, serious medical consequences, and delirium, I had to learn how to live again. I have been sober for ten years.

For a long time, I could not see what my family had already lived through

During the years I drank, I made promises, explained things away, and convinced myself I was still in control. Meanwhile, the people around me watched, worried, adapted, and tried to hold together what kept falling apart.

Sobriety did not erase any of that. Stopping drinking was only the first step. Trust, responsibility, and relationships had to be rebuilt slowly.

Why speak to family members?

Stories about addiction often keep all attention on the person who drinks. But the people beside them have a story, too—their own losses, boundaries, safety, and life. 621 SOBER does not teach you to control someone else. It invites you to notice yourself again.

What I promise

I share lived experience honestly without presenting it as universal truth. I use plain language, respect each family member’s choices, and point clearly toward professional or emergency help when needed.

Why 621?

The name comes from the numbers that marked my history: six attacks of pancreatitis, two seizures, and one delirium—followed by ten years of sobriety. Today the name stands not only for what happened to me, but also for the work I now offer families.
